newsitem.title: USA: TWA says prince done buying stock for now.
newsitem.headline: TWA says prince done buying stock for now.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said Wednesday that Saudi Arabia's Prince Al-Waleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud told the carrier he has no plans to purchase additional shares in the company at this point.
Earlier Wednesday, the prince called TWA Chairman Gerald Gitner and said he had purchased about five percent or 2,088,000 shares of the company's common stock.
TWA said the prince also said he is hopeful that management will succeed in its effort of bringing TWA to long-term profitability.

The prince has built a multi-billion dollar business empire with interests in construction, real estate, banking, travel, broadcast media, supermarkets and other sectors. His investments include shares in Citicorp and Euro Disney.
On Tuesday, TWA, the seventh largest U.S. air carrier, reported a 1996 year-end loss of $284.8 million including special charges of $85.9 million on revenues of $3.55 billion.
At that time, TWA also outlined actions to revive the carrier's restructuring plan which stalled in 1996.
Shares of TWA were trading up 1/8 to seven.
